🐛 Fix `on_startup` and `on_shutdown` parameters of `APIRouter`

This fixes the issue reported in this comment: https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/pull/14851#issuecomment-3863896385

```py
from fastapi import FastAPI


def s_start():
    print("SYNC START", flush=True)


app = FastAPI(on_startup=[s_start])


@app.get("/health")
async def health():
    return {"ok": True}
```

steps.message: The fix was to move the initialization of `self.on_startup` and `self.on_shutdown` in `APIRouter.__init__` to occur after the call to `super().__init__`, preventing the superclass from overriding these attributes.

The bug was caused by the `on_startup` and `on_shutdown` attributes being assigned in `APIRouter.__init__` before the call to `super().__init__`. Since `APIRouter` inherits from Starlette's `Router`, the superclass's initialization was overriding these attributes, effectively erasing the user-provided startup and shutdown handlers. The fix moves the assignment of `self.on_startup` and `self.on_shutdown` to occur after the `super().__init__` call.
